prompt:
Refine image 1 into the final, fully in-game-looking Tower Codex interface for Copilot Hub. Use case: ui-mockup, precise game screen refinement. Landscape 16:9, crisp high-resolution production screenshot appearance, no presentation border, no concept labels.
REFERENCE PRIORITY: image 1 supplies the chosen composition, physical portrait noticeboard at left, live Developer model center, stats at right, interior counter and park through the windows. Retain this chosen Codex concept. Image 2 supplies actual Hub renderer/style. Image 3 supplies actual central Lab architecture/palette. Image 4 is the canonical Developer model and must remain recognizable without redesign. Image 5 supplies the actual campus noticeboard construction. The entire interface should look like it was captured running inside the same simple Three.js low-poly game as the Hub, not an artist's cinematic rendering of a future game.
USER-REQUIRED CHANGES:
1. ANIMATION SELECTION ONLY. Remove the entire bottom transport area: absolutely no playback slider, scrubber, timeline, play icon, pause icon, speed dropdown, replay control, loop toggle or "1×". Replace it with ONE calm row of seven selectable animation chips labelled exactly "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve". Idle alone is selected with the same subdued mint fill used by the actual Hub's camera toggle. Selecting a chip is all the user needs to do to preview its animation. Put the label "ANIMATION" above/beside this compact strip. Recover the old slider's space to improve overall spacing.
2. VISUAL STATS ONLY. The right-hand display has icons, short labels and horizontal segmented meters only. Remove ALL numeric stat values, price figures, units, multipliers, percentages, totals, fractions and numerical labels everywhere. In particular remove "7", "5", "2.5", "20", "30", "50", "/ action", "/ sec", "units", "Base 30 · Total 50", "+20 Compute". No digits should be visible anywhere in the interface. No numeric tick labels, numerical tooltips or hidden mini price badges. Keep the labels exactly "Damage", "Work", "Action speed", "Range". Gauge fills: Damage just under halfway; Work full; Action speed full; Range around two-thirds. Beneath these show a small separate "Compute" label with a chip icon and a restrained amber expenditure meter, mostly filled, with NO numbers. Reuse one consistent graphic vocabulary, not a radar chart. All other stat meters use muted mint/blue consistent with the Hub. Header "STATS". Remove the "Playtest stats" development badge entirely; this is the player-facing game screen.
IN-GAME STYLE PASS: Match the actual Hub's flat solid matte colors, small simple bevels, modest shadowing, chunky/faceted geometry, restrained navy and pale-mint HUD. Off-white lab slabs, blue-gray frames, soft cyan windows; broad neutral daylight, no golden tint, no polished reflections, no cinematic depth of field or background bokeh, no realistic material textures, no dramatic bloom. Simplify bulky layered beveled panels into thin slabs like the actual campus props. UI type is the current Hub's clear modest sans serif. Stat and animation text should be flat and readable as live game UI, not perspective-warped texture lettering. Preserve visual depth in the physical counter and noticeboard. No browser/page chrome, no generic website grid or dashboard, no ornamental armored sci-fi corners, no trading-card stars or rarity rankings, no new logo design.
Keep selected title "Developer" and role "Direct-output specialist". Keep the seven character dossiers "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter", selected Developer with a narrow mint edge. The actual orange Developer is a hovering HEAD ONLY, orange faceted spikes, chunky dark goggles with teal lenses, black face with exactly two cyan vertical eyes, cream ear pods with curly-brace glyph; no body or new accessories. Other known models in portraits keep their original purple/blue/yellow identities; missing-model cards keep quiet silhouettes. The hero Developer is actually modelled and lit in the scene, not a flat card illustration.
Keep model rotation/tilt gesture arrows and a small camera reset icon; these are camera controls, not animation playback. Small hint "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom". A faint unnumbered radius ring below the model is fine, no large holographic bloom.
Header: existing Copilot wordmark text "COPILOT" and "TOWER DEFENSE"; location/subheading "COPILOT HUB / TOWER CODEX". Clear simple "Back to Hub" control top right. No taglines, no fictional quotes or extra copy. Show the nearby paths, faceted trees and benches through the window, consistent with being inside the central Lab; never show another copy of the same central Lab outside. Every element should feel part of the existing Hub world. Keep the scene composed and operable, with the model, roster and visual stats clearly separated by space and architecture rather than webapp boxes.
